visuals.title: Which path is a screening exam?
visuals.prompt: A patient has no breast symptoms and is here for routine annual imaging. Select the path that matches a screening mammogram.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Right path: symptoms or abnormal screen, individualized views

feedback.a: Correct. Screening uses routine views in an asymptomatic patient.
feedback.b: That path is diagnostic—used for symptoms, signs, or an abnormal screening finding.

visuals.explanation: NCI and MQSA audit language agree: screening is for asymptomatic routine imaging; diagnostic exams individualize views for symptoms, signs, or abnormal screening findings.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Paths are announced by purpose and view type; selecting either path is fully keyboard accessible.

visuals.title: Which categories trigger dense notification?
visuals.prompt: Select the least dense category that maps to the patient statement 'Your breast tissue is dense.'

feedback.a: Almost entirely fatty maps to not dense.
feedback.b: Scattered fibroglandular density still maps to not dense.
feedback.c: Correct. Heterogeneously dense is the lower of the two dense categories.
feedback.d: Extremely dense is dense, but it is not the least dense category that triggers the dense statement.

visuals.explanation: MQSA maps the first two report categories to 'not dense' and heterogeneously/extremely dense to 'dense.' NCI uses the same dense threshold for patient letters.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Category names are visible on the schematic; the dense/not-dense mapping is revealed after answering.

visuals.title: Who individualizes density follow-up advice?
visuals.prompt: A patient asks whether she should add ultrasound because her letter said her tissue is dense. Select who should individualize that recommendation.

hotspots.revealLabel: Technologist: process, comfort, MQSA timelines—not individualized supplemental screening orders

hotspots.neutralLabel: Column B: Written reports / interpreting physician role
hotspots.revealLabel: Written MQSA reports and density statements
Referring clinician: individual risk and supplemental testing discussion

feedback.a: Technologists can explain that dense tissue is common and that the lay letter comes from the facility, but they should not invent a personal ultrasound/MRI plan.
feedback.b: Reports carry required density language, but personalized next steps belong with the patient's clinician.
feedback.c: Correct. NCI and USPSTF point patients to talk with their clinician about options when evidence for supplemental screening is insufficient.

visuals.explanation: MQSA requires density notification in the lay summary. Supplemental imaging decisions are individualized clinical counseling, not a technologist diagnosis.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Columns are named by role; contents after reveal do not change the keyboard choices.

visuals.title: What must the infection-control system address?
visuals.prompt: After contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials, MQSA requires documented cleaning of mammography equipment. Select the schematic zone that includes the compression paddle contacting the breast.

hotspots.revealLabel: Tube housing (not the primary patient-contact paddle)
Breast support / receptor cover — also a contact surface

hotspots.neutralLabel: Zone D, floor under the unit
hotspots.revealLabel: Floor — facility housekeeping, not the MQSA equipment-contact rule itself

feedback.a: The tube housing is not the patient-contact paddle surface highlighted by this question.
feedback.b: Correct. The paddle contacts the breast; MQSA requires procedures for cleaning equipment after blood/OPIM contact, following regulations and manufacturer guidance.
feedback.c: The support is also a contact surface, but this prompt asked specifically for the compression paddle zone.
feedback.d: Floor cleaning matters in a clinic, but MQSA § 900.12(e)(13) is about mammography equipment after blood/OPIM contact.

visuals.explanation: MQSA infection control is a documented system for cleaning and disinfecting mammography equipment after blood or OPIM contact, aligned with applicable regulations and manufacturer recommendations.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Zones are described by position; names appear after answering.

glossary.definition: Routine mammographic views of an asymptomatic patient (MQSA audit definition); used to look for cancer before symptoms.
Individualized mammographic views for symptoms, physical signs, or abnormal screening findings; often more angles than screening.
MQSA-required easy-to-read written results for the patient, including a density statement, within required timelines.
Heterogeneously dense or extremely dense tissue on mammography; common; increases masking and is a risk factor; not palpable on exam.
3D mammography that acquires thin-slice images assembled into a volumetric picture and also produces 2D images.
Materials other than blood that may contain bloodborne pathogens; MQSA requires equipment cleaning procedures after contact with blood or OPIM.
Employer plan under OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard describing how the workplace will reduce occupational exposure.
Special mammographic technique used when implants are present to show more native breast tissue; patients should tell the facility about implants beforehand.
